purpose: Registry of authoritative source documents. Every rule in rules.*.json must point to a source_id here. Nothing may be asserted to a student unless its source is listed, its verification_status is not 'unverified', and the student's programme level falls inside the source's declared scope.
institution: The Education University of Hong Kong (EdUHK)
snapshot_policy: Sources are captured as immutable snapshots. If the University revises a page, add a NEW source entry with a new version and retrieved_date. Never edit an old snapshot in place.

scope_model.why: EdUHK does not publish one set of academic regulations. It publishes separate documents for different programme types, and at least one of them is split by intake year. A clause that governs a BEd student may not govern a taught master's student, and the clause numbers may not even line up. Scope is therefore a required field, not metadata: applying a clause outside its scope is a correctness failure even when the wording is quoted perfectly.

programme_levels.rpg: Research postgraduate (MPhil, PhD) and professional doctorate (EdD)

scope_fields.programme_levels: Which programme levels this document governs. Empty array means the scope is not yet established.
scope_fields.cohort_from: First intake year the document applies to, e.g. '2014/15'. null means no lower bound is stated.
scope_fields.cohort_to: Last intake year, e.g. '2013/14'. null means the document is current.
scope_fields.scope_basis: verbatim = the document states its own scope. inferred_from_structure = the author deduced the scope from the existence of sibling documents. needs_confirmation = not established; may not be asserted.

scope_model.inheritance: A rule inherits the scope of its source document. A rule may override with its own 'scope' object only when the source document states the narrower scope explicitly.

known_gaps.student_facing_summary: You have not yet said what the email is for, so no clause can be selected. The regulations are organised by topic — deadlines, grades, absence, review — and a clause cannot be applied to a request that has not been described. The draft asks which procedure applies, and names none.
known_gaps.consequence_for_product: This is an empty state by design, not a corpus gap. It must not be reported as a finding about the University.
known_gaps.action_required: None. If a student reaches this state often, that is a signal about the question flow, not about the policy base.

known_gaps.description: The corpus covers one of at least three regulation families. EdUHK publishes (a) General Academic Regulations in the Student Handbook, (b) General Academic Regulations for Taught Postgraduate Programmes in two intake-year versions (2013/14 and before; 2014/15 and thereafter), and (c) General Academic Regulations for the Research Component for RPg and professional doctorate programmes. The 2026/27 handbook preface also directs students to consult their programme handbook and programme materials, which may add requirements the central regulations do not contain.
known_gaps.consequence_for_product: A single-policy-base design would silently apply undergraduate clauses to postgraduate students. Scope is therefore modelled as a required field on every source and every rule, and the Gatekeeper withholds rather than substitutes when the student's programme is outside the collected corpus.
known_gaps.action_required: Retrieve the TPG regulations (both cohort versions) and the research-component regulations, then register them as new sources. Until then, TPG and RPg students must receive the scope-gap state, not a borrowed clause.

known_gaps.student_facing_summary: The central academic regulations do not set out a procedure for missing an examination. They set out what happens to a grade when an absence is not approved (GAR 13.2), and how to apply for leave (GAR 13.1), but the examination-absence procedure itself sits in course and programme documents.
known_gaps.description: The General Academic Regulations do not contain a standalone 'absence from examination' clause. Absence is handled through GAR 13.1 (leave of absence), 13.2 (unapproved absence => grade F) and course-level assessment schemes (13.3).
known_gaps.consequence_for_product: An 'exam' request cannot be answered from the central handbook alone. The Gatekeeper must route the student to the course/programme assessment scheme and state that the rule is course-specific rather than inventing a University-wide procedure.
known_gaps.action_required: Collect at least two programme/course assessment schemes to see how they specify exam absence.
known_gaps.partial_mitigation: For students registered with the Student Affairs Office, 'Special Examination Arrangements' (extended time, assistive equipment, enlarged papers, supervised breaks, modified response formats) are listed as an SEN support service — see EDUHK-SAO-SEN-WEB-2026 for the full list. Additionally, 'Extension of assignment deadlines' is explicitly listed under Lecture/Assignment Arrangements on the same page. These are accommodation routes, not absence procedures, and the two must not be conflated in the UI. The remaining open question is whether any accommodation can be arranged retrospectively (after a deadline or exam has passed).

known_gaps.description: No standalone 'extenuating circumstances' or 'special consideration' policy was found in the central regulations. Special circumstances appear only as a ground for formal grade review (GAR 9.2.2(iii)) and as leave of absence (GAR 13.1). The supervisor has confirmed that EdUHK has no faculty-level special consideration mechanism outside the handbook.
known_gaps.consequence_for_product: This is a genuine finding, not a defect in the search. State it explicitly in the report: the student-facing consequence is that after a deadline has passed, there is no clean 'ask for an extension' route in the central regulations. However, the SAO SEN Support Services web page (EDUHK-SAO-SEN-WEB-2026, retrieved 2026-11-09) explicitly lists 'Extension of assignment deadlines' as a possible reasonable accommodation for students with SEN. This means the route through the lecturer is closed, but a SEN support route for assignment deadline extensions IS available for eligible students.
known_gaps.action_required: None outstanding. Report this as a confirmed institutional finding: no central regulation, but a SEN support service explicitly covers the gap.

supplementary_finding.finding: The SAO support service page lists 'Extension of assignment deadlines' under Lecture/Assignment Arrangements as a possible reasonable accommodation.

known_gaps.description: Previously an open question: whether EdUHK has an established procedure for using AI tools in the capstone project, and whether an approved LLM service is available without purchasing an external API. Both questions are now answered.
known_gaps.resolution: The reimbursement scheme (EDUHK-REIMBURSEMENT-2026) IS the established procedure. Under its framework, the project supervisor's pre-approval constitutes the complete procedural requirement for AI tool use in the capstone project. No separate LTTC application is needed. LTTC does provide an approved LLM service (LLM Studio / MaaS platform), but access is structured through workshops and credit-bearing courses, not a public no-registration chat interface.
known_gaps.consequence_for_product: The project may proceed with AI integration under the supervisor's pre-approval. If the model uses LTTC's LLM Studio, the access model (workshops/courses) must be accounted for. If the model uses an external API, the reimbursement scheme covers it up to HK$5,000, but only if the tool is not available from LTTC. The template-based baseline remains the zero-hallucination control condition regardless of which model path is chosen.
known_gaps.action_required: None. Record in the report as a resolved decision point.
